quote: In Louisville, at the corner of Fourth and Walnut, in the center of the shopping district, I was suddenly overwhelmed with the realization that I loved all those people, that they were mine and I theirs, that we could not be alien to one another even though we were total strangers.
source: Thomas Merton, Conjectures of a Guilty Bystander, Part Three, The Night Spirit and the Dawn Air (Doubleday, 1966)

evidence.where: Open Library search inside, where more than a dozen books quote the sentence in this wording, and a bibliography of Merton that places the passage in The Night Spirit and the Dawn Air in Conjectures
evidence.edition: Conjectures of a Guilty Bystander, Doubleday, Garden City, 1966
evidence.locator: Part Three, The Night Spirit and the Dawn Air, the reworking of the journal entry of 18 March 1958, commonly cited at pp. 140 to 142

reason: The sentence is the published wording, not the journal draft, and reads all those people in every witness that quotes the book; the all these people seen on quotation sites is a slip. The five parts of Conjectures run Barth’s Dream, Truth and Violence, The Night Spirit and the Dawn Air, The Fork in the Road, The Madman Runs to the East, so Part Three is right. The page was left out because no scan could be opened to confirm it. Merton is unshipped, unbanned and at zero for the year.
